landing.heroSubtitle: Orchestrate 10 professional cybersecurity tools in an 11-phase pipeline. From reconnaissance to exploitation — with CVSS/EPSS scoring and pentest-style reports.
landing.feature1Desc: Intelligent 11-step pipeline: Wappalyzer, Nmap, Patator, Metasploit, ffuf, Gobuster, ZAP, Nuclei, SQLMap and Searchsploit run in coordinated sequence.
landing.feature2Desc: DAST analysis with OWASP ZAP and automatic correlation with Exploit-DB. CVSS v3.1/v4.0 and EPSS scoring for risk prioritization.
landing.feature3Desc: Discover ports, services, versions and OS with Nmap and NSE scripts. Full technology stack fingerprinting.
landing.feature4Desc: Offline Exploit-DB search with Searchsploit. Each CVE correlates with the software versions detected during reconnaissance.
landing.feature5Desc: Authentication cookies captured by Patator propagate to ZAP, Nuclei and SQLMap — authenticated scans cover 100% of the surface.
landing.feature6Desc: Pentest reports exportable as HTML, PDF, JSON and CSV. Includes a global risk score, severity breakdown and per-tool evidence.
landing.toolsSubtitle: 10 professional tools coordinated in an automated pipeline
landing.tool1Details: Wappalyzer detects the technologies the target uses: CMS, frontend and backend frameworks, web servers, JavaScript libraries and e-commerce platforms. It's the first pipeline step — its output guides every following phase and feeds Searchsploit's exploit search.
landing.tool2Details: Industry standard for network discovery. Scans TCP/UDP ports, detects active services, identifies software versions and runs NSE scripts to grab banners, SSL certificates and exposed configurations.
landing.tool3Details: Modular brute-force tool. Tests credentials against HTTP/HTTPS forms, Basic/Digest authentication, SSH and FTP. Captured cookies propagate to ZAP, Nuclei and SQLMap for full authenticated scans.
landing.tool4Details: Runs in controlled mode via the RPC daemon (msfrpcd). Only launches auxiliary verification modules — no destructive exploits — to confirm whether detected vulnerabilities are actually exploitable on the target.
landing.tool5Details: Web fuzzer written in Go — extremely fast. Discovers hidden content, fuzzes GET/POST parameters, identifies virtual hosts (vhosts) and enumerates undocumented API endpoints with support for multiple wordlists.
landing.tool6Details: Discovers hidden routes and files on web servers through wordlist-based brute force. Finds admin panels, exposed configuration files and unlinked API endpoints.
landing.tool7Desc: Full DAST with Spider and Active Scan
landing.tool7Details: The world's most widely used web security scanner. Crawls the site with its Spider, then runs an Active Scan that tests every parameter for SQLi, XSS, CSRF, command injection and 40+ attack types from the OWASP catalog.
landing.tool8Details: Runs scans using community YAML templates. Covers known CVEs, misconfigurations, exposed panels and outdated technologies. Its public library has thousands of continuously updated templates.
landing.tool9Details: Automates SQL injection detection and exploitation. Supports all types (blind, error-based, time-based, UNION) and multiple engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL and Oracle. Runs against parameters discovered by ZAP and ffuf.
landing.tool10Details: CLI interface for Exploit-DB. Searches public exploits offline using the versions detected by Wappalyzer and Nmap. Each result includes the local path to the exploit code and its CVE reference for vulnerability correlation.
landing.workflowSubtitle: Optimized 10-phase sequence with intelligent orchestration and session propagation
landing.labsSubtitle: Intentionally vulnerable applications. Practice safely and legally.
landing.lab1Desc: Node.js app with 100+ challenges. Covers OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities in realistic scenarios.
landing.lab2Desc: Damn Vulnerable Web Application. Classic environment for practicing SQLi, XSS, CSRF, File Upload and more.
landing.lab3Desc: Interactive OWASP tutorials with guided lessons on common web vulnerabilities.
landing.ctaFinalSubtitle: Run your first full scan with the v5.0 stack. Results in minutes, a professional report ready to present.
landing.legalNotice: For ethical and authorized use only · Colombian Law 1273/2009
landing.footerTagline: SENA Academic Project · For ethical and authorized use only

docs.pageSubtitle: Complete guide to SecureScan Pro v5.0 tools and API
docs.tool1Desc: Full technology stack fingerprinting. Detects CMS, frameworks, web servers, JS libraries and e-commerce platforms.
docs.tool2Desc: The world's most popular network scanner. Discovers hosts, ports, services, versions and operating systems.
docs.tool3Desc: Modular, multi-purpose brute-force tool. Supports HTTP, SSH, FTP, SMTP and more protocols.
docs.tool4Desc: Penetration testing framework for controlled exploit validation via RPC daemon. Requires explicit authorization.
docs.tool4Feature1: Thousands of exploit and auxiliary modules
docs.tool5Desc: High-speed web fuzzer written in Go. Ideal for content, parameter and virtual host discovery.
docs.tool5Feature4: Filtering by size, words or status
docs.tool6Desc: Brute-force tool for discovering directories, files, subdomains and vhosts on web servers.
docs.tool7Desc: Comprehensive security proxy for DAST. Traditional Spider, Ajax Spider, active scan and vulnerability fuzzing.
docs.tool8Desc: Vulnerability scanner based on community YAML templates. Covers CVEs, misconfigurations and exposed panels.
docs.tool9Desc: Automated tool for SQL injection detection and exploitation. Supports all SQLi types and multiple DBMS.
docs.tool9Feature1: Automatic SQLi detection (blind, error, time-based, UNION)
docs.tool9Feature2: Support for MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, Oracle
docs.tool9Feature5: Integration with endpoints discovered by ZAP and ffuf
docs.tool10Desc: CLI interface for the Exploit-DB database. Offline exploit search by service/version with CVE reference.
docs.tool10Feature2: Offline search, no internet connection needed
docs.tool10Feature5: Integration with versions detected by Wappalyzer and Nmap
docs.zapSpiderDesc: OWASP ZAP's spider: crawls the application and discovers URLs, paths and forms. In SecureScan it runs before the active scan as part of the ZAP full scan, and its URLs are listed in the Pentesting results.
docs.zapSpiderFeature1: Discovers URLs and paths by crawling the application
docs.zapSpiderFeature2: Runs before the active scan inside the ZAP full scan
docs.zapSpiderFeature3: Discovered URLs are shown in the ZAP Spider tab
docs.injectionScannerDesc: SecureScan Pro's own module that detects 10 injection types with active payloads. It runs in the SQLMap step; if the module isn't available, the backend falls back to SQLMap.
docs.injectionScannerFeature1: 10 techniques: SQLi, NoSQLi, XPath, XXE, XSS, command injection, path traversal (LFI), SSRF, SSTI and LDAP
docs.injectionScannerFeature2: SQLi as error-based, UNION, boolean-blind, time-blind, auth bypass, stacked and second-order
docs.injectionScannerFeature3: Built for Juice Shop, DVWA and WebGoat; basic detection on forms of other targets
docs.injectionScannerFeature4: Can use the session cookie obtained by Patator
docs.crtshDesc: Discovers subdomains from public Certificate Transparency logs by querying crt.sh. No API key required. It may list old subdomains that no longer resolve.
docs.crtshFeature1: Unique subdomains and number of certificates found
docs.crtshFeature3: If the target is an IP, it tries a reverse DNS (PTR) lookup to get a domain
docs.dnstwistDesc: Detects typosquatting and phishing domains similar to the target using the real dnstwist library (14 techniques, including homoglyphs and bitsquatting) and resolves which ones are registered. It caps the number of variants to keep runtime reasonable.
docs.dnstwistFeature1: Lists similar domains that are already registered, with their IP
docs.dnstwistFeature2: Reports how many variants were checked
docs.dnstwistFeature3: If the target is an IP, it first tries a reverse DNS lookup to find a hostname
docs.shodanDesc: External exposure via Shodan InternetDB (free, no API key): open ports, hostnames, CPEs, tags and CVEs associated with the IP. It only works with IPs; a domain target is resolved via DNS.
docs.shodanFeature1: Open ports and known hostnames of the IP
docs.shodanFeature2: CVEs inferred from the banner version: may be false positives if the service is patched
docs.shodanFeature3: Tags such as cdn, vpn, tor or compromised
docs.shodanFeature4: No API key required; InternetDB data isn't real-time
docs.virustotalDesc: Queries the report VirusTotal already has for the domain or IP (API v3); it does not scan the target. Requires the VIRUSTOTAL_API_KEY variable on the server: without it the result is marked as no real data.
docs.virustotalFeature1: Engine verdicts: malicious, suspicious, harmless and undetected
docs.virustotalFeature2: List of engines that flagged the target
docs.virustotalFeature3: Link to the full report on VirusTotal
docs.abuseipdbDesc: IP reputation on AbuseIPDB (API v2). It only works with IPs: a domain is resolved via DNS and the resulting IP is reported. Requires the ABUSEIPDB_API_KEY variable on the server.
docs.abuseipdbFeature1: Abuse confidence score (0–100) and number of reports
docs.abuseipdbFeature2: Country, ISP and usage type of the IP
docs.abuseipdbFeature3: Date of the last report and a link to the AbuseIPDB detail
docs.safebrowsingDesc: Checks whether Google Safe Browsing already flags the URL as malware, social engineering (phishing) or unwanted software. Requires the GOOGLE_SAFE_BROWSING_API_KEY variable on the server.
docs.safebrowsingFeature1: Tells whether the URL is flagged as a threat
docs.testsslDesc: Analyzes the target's TLS/SSL configuration with testssl.sh: offered protocols, known vulnerabilities and certificate data. It connects directly to the target's port.
docs.testsslFeature1: Offered protocols (SSLv3, TLS 1.0–1.3) with their severity
docs.testsslFeature3: Certificate data: subject, expiry, key size and signature algorithm
docs.testsslFeature4: If the port doesn't speak TLS or the analysis times out, it is reported as an error
